sources.citation: Fajaryanto, Galang. 2020. A phonological analysis of palatalization in the Osing dialect of Javanese, Banyuwangi. MA thesis (Linguistics), Universitas Diponegoro, Semarang. 152 pp. (CORE 365579888)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No rule for word stress; only an incidental PRAAT remark (p. 54) that [i]/[I] as syllable peaks 'usually [have] stressed intonation'. Phoneme inventory, syllable structure and palatalization rule only.

sources.citation: Nurhayani, Ika; Hamamah; Mardiana, Dwi I.N.A; Delijar, Ressi M. 2020. Looking into the language status of Osing with a contrastive analysis of the basic vocabulary of Osing and Malang Javanese. Parole: Journal of Linguistics and Education 10(2): 87-96. doi:10.14710/parole.v10i2.87-96
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental correspondences (palatalization, word-final diphthongs, final glottal stop) between Osing and Malang Javanese; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Delijar, Ressi Maulidina. 2019. Phonological errors in pronouncing Basa Osing: analysis of language behavior. NOTION: Journal of Linguistics, Literature, and Culture 1(2). doi:10.12928/notion.v1i2.860 (CORE 490597992)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Osing features (7 vowel phonemes; /i u/ in open ultima -> [ai au], in closed ultima -> [E O]; geminate-like /w j r l/; palatalization), citing Wedhawati 2006 and Jusuf & Noor 2016; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wittke, Jonas. 2019. Status Planning and Regional Identity: The Case of Osing in Banyuwangi, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, Rice University. 154 pp. (hdl 1911/105415)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 2 summarises Osing segmental phonology after Herusantosa (1987: 92-106) and Hasan Ali (2006): six vowel phonemes/ten allophones as in Javanese, word-final /i u/ -> [ai au] 'not just word-finally, but also phrase- or sentence-finally', palatalization of voiced C before [a]/[E]; quantitative study of these variables. No statement about word stress or accent anywhere (no hits for stress/accent/penult).

sources.citation: Franendya, Retno Ajeng. 2014. Phonological and lexical exploration on dialect differences between Kemiren and Tampo Osing. S1 thesis and article, Universitas Brawijaya, Malang. (CORE 290400125, 537832608)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sound correspondences between two Osing village varieties; silent on stress placement.

sources.citation: Arps, Bernard. 2010. Terwujudnya bahasa Using di Banyuwangi dan peranan media elektronik di dalamnya (selayang pandang, 1970-2009). In M. Moriyama & M. Budiman (eds), Geliat bahasa selaras zaman, 225-248. Tokyo: ILCAA. (CORE 388689876)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic history of the recognition/standardisation of Using; no phonology. Bibliography identifies the primary descriptions: Herusantosa 1987 (UI dissertation), Hasan Ali [1997] Tata bahasa baku bahasa Using jilid 1 ('membahas fonologi'), Hasan Ali 2002 Kamus bahasa daerah Using-Indonesia (+40 pp. spelling guide), Endro Wilis 2001.

sources.citation: Mas Moeljono, Koentjahjo, Sri Wahyu Widayati & Leo Indra Ardiana. 1986. Tingkat Tutur Bahasa Jawa Dialek Banyuwangi. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. 111 pp. (CORE 227146761)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Speech-level study; silent on stress (one incidental mention of 'intonasi').

sources.citation: Sugono, Dendy. 1985. Verba transitif dialek Osing: analisis tagmemik. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xiv+81 pp. (Glottolog ref 9291; Internet Archive copy of repositori.kemdikbud.go.id/29434)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: No Osing stress statement; only a generic tagmemic remark (p. 21) that the Indonesian clitic -mu 'tidak pernah mendapat tekanan'. Literature review (pp. 2-3) names earlier structural work: Koentamadi 1972 (phonology paper, Seminar Bahasa Daerah 1974), Sudjito dkk 1978 'Struktur Dialek Banyuwangi' (report with fonologi chapter), Soetoko dkk 1979/1981.

sources.citation: Soetoko, Soekarto, Abd. Rozak Zaidan, Busyairi & Hadiri. 1981. Geografi Dialek Banyuwangi. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. 197 pp. (CORE 227145033)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. States that the Banyuwangi dialect differs from ordinary Javanese in 'kosa kata, fonem, morfem, intonasi' and that 'Intonasi dialek Banyuwangi menimbulkan kekhasan bahasa itu' (pp. 44-45), then under 4.1 Hambatan: 'Keragaman intonasi DB sebenarnya perlu dipetakan. Akan tetapi, berhubung dengan tidak adanya alat yang memadai untuk keperluan itu, maka hal itu tidak dilakukan.' No 'tekanan'/'aksen' anywhere in the text layer.

sources.citation: Sudjito dkk. 1978 [1979]. Struktur Dialek Banyuwangi. Laporan penelitian, Proyek Penelitian Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia dan Daerah Jawa Timur / Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa (naskah, tidak diterbitkan).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Earliest structural sketch with a fonologi chapter (reviewed in Sugono 1985: 2-3); Pusat Bahasa 'Struktur' reports usually include a paragraph on tekanan.

sources.citation: Hasan Ali. 2006. Tata Bahasa Baku Bahasa Using. Banyuwangi: Pemerintah Kabupaten Banyuwangi. (1st part issued [1997] as Tata bahasa baku bahasa Using, Jilid 1 = fonologi.)

sources.note: Normative grammar whose first volume is devoted to phonology; prescriptive works of this kind routinely state where 'tekanan kata' falls and it is the source Wittke quotes for the phrase-final diphthong rule.
